_note: Health and day-intensity tuning (GDD 4.5–4.6). The health model (HealthSystem) reads everything below; injuries and illnesses themselves are in data/injuries.json, session strain in data/training.json. Strain is a hidden number per body area (0 = fresh, ~30 a bit sore, ~50 sore, ~70 painful).

intensity._note: Per-day intensity (this week's day changes). load = multiplier on the fatigue a session adds; effect = multiplier on its training stimulus; strain = multiplier on the body strain it adds. Normal must stay 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.0 so the weekly plan behaves as before. Races ignore intensity.

easy.name: Easy
easy.description: Run the sessions gently: less tiring, a bit less training effect.

hard.name: Hard
hard.description: Push harder than planned: a bit more training effect, but much more tiring.

areas._note: The six body areas, in a fixed order. keep = share of the strain still there the next day (bone fades slowly, muscle fast).

list.name: Shins
list.helps: Less running on hard roads, fewer long runs for a while, softer surfaces, and a gradual build-up.

list.name: Feet
list.helps: Less running volume for a few days, softer surfaces, and calf stretching.

list.name: Knees
list.helps: Fewer hill sprints and bounding drills, and an easier day or two.

list.name: Heels & Achilles
list.helps: No hills or fast running for a few days, and calf exercises.

list.name: Hamstrings
list.helps: No sprinting until it feels loose again, and mobility work.

list.name: Calves
list.helps: A couple of easy days without fast running, and mobility work.

soreness._note: How strain shows to the player. levels = strain where 'a bit sore', 'sore' and 'painful' start. (Step 5: 'a bit sore' moved from 30 to 34 so the recommended coach plan is no longer 'a bit sore' on 4 days out of 10; the injury risk curve below is unchanged.)

ui._note: Display only (M2 step 4, the health UI): nothing here changes the model. load_cap = 'load vs your normal' is shown as 'over N %' above this; load_low / load_high = the percentages where the words change (a lighter week / a step up above data strain.spike.free_ratio / a big jump). soreness_hints = the one-line advice shown with each soreness level.
soreness_hints: An early warning. This is the cheapest moment to ease off: a lighter day or two now usually stops it turning into a real problem.
Your body is asking for a break. Training on through this is how most running injuries start.
Painful: this area is close to giving way. Rest it. If you carry on, expect it to become an injury.

strain._note: What adds strain on top of the session's own numbers, and what makes it fade faster. Every multiplier is 1.0 for an average athlete on a normal day.
strain._fatigue_note: Tired legs: ×(1 + fatigue_extra × (fatigue − fatigue_from) / (100 − fatigue_from)) above fatigue_from.
strain._hard_surface_note: Track sessions done on roads/snow in winter (no indoor hall) hit these areas harder.
strain._fade_note: Each point of recovery rate / professionalism above 10 takes this much off 'keep' (below 10 adds it).

spike._note: Acute vs chronic load (impact = the strain sessions add before multipliers). The body adapts to its last ~4 weeks: an acute:chronic ratio above free_ratio adds per_ratio × (ratio − free_ratio) to every area's strain, up to max. A new career starts as if it had done start_daily_impact a day (about the coach plan).

adaptation._note: Capacity: a body used to more load takes each session better. Strain added is divided by the capacity, which follows (chronic daily impact / start_daily_impact)^power (kept between min and max) slowly: bone and tendon need weeks to adapt. Each day it moves 1/days_up of the way up or 1/days_down of the way down. So a gradual build-up to a hard plan is safe, a sudden jump isn't, and weeks off make the body lose it again.

growth._note: Growth spurt: peak at this age (gender) shifted by maturation; within half_width years of it the listed areas take up to ×(1 + extra) strain.

history._note: A past injury makes its area take up to ×(1 + extra) strain, fading over this many days after it healed.

injury_risk._note: Daily overuse-injury chance per area: at_sore × 2^((strain − sore_strain) / doubling): it doubles every `doubling` points of strain. Zero below zero_below, fading in up to full_from (so near zero below 'a bit sore'). × hidden injury proneness (1 → proneness[0], 20 → proneness[1]); girls × female_bone in bone areas. When it hits, the injury is picked from the catalogue: candidates whose min_strain is reached, weight × (1 + (strain − min_strain) / pick_bias) so overloaded areas give worse injuries.

acute._note: Bad luck per session: the session's own 'acute' chances (data/training.json), × (1 + fatigue_extra × (fatigue − 30) / 70) when tired, × proneness. Running on icy roads in winter (road sessions, and track sessions done off-track) adds an ankle-sprain chance.

escalation._note: Daily chance that an injury that can get worse (escalates_to) does: after a day trained through its limits (a banned session done), after racing on it, or when its area is painful anyway. The trained-through and raced chances are × (area strain / 'sore' level)², kept between strain_min and strain_max, so training through on a calm area is a smaller gamble. Each day an injury (not an illness) is trained through also adds extend_days to its current phase.

illness._note: Daily chance of falling ill (then cold or flu by catalogue weight): daily × month_weight (Jan..Dec) × tiredness × after a race × professionalism (1 → professionalism[0], 20 → professionalism[1]).

warning._note: The 'sore' stop event comes when an area turns sore, at most once per area in this many days.

detraining._note: Extra loss for every physical attribute that got no training stimulus this week, per day beyond after_days in a row with no training at all.

running_detraining._note: Running-specific fitness fades without running even when cross-training keeps the aerobic engine (aqua jogging, bike and swimming maintain VO2max for weeks, but not speed endurance, economy, threshold pace or top speed). Per day beyond after_days in a row without a running session or race (session tag 'run'), applied at the end of the week. Not permanent: training builds it back.

plan_risk._note: The weekly plan's risk word: expected overuse injuries over `weeks` weeks of it from the current body state (average proneness, so it never gives the hidden value away).

proneness_hint._note: After this many injuries (not illnesses) within this many days, the game hints that the athlete picks up knocks easily.

rivals._note: Each week a fit rival has this chance to get injured and miss training and races for a number of weeks drawn inside `weeks`.

restrictions._note: What an injury phase allows. bans = session tags (data/training.json) that can't be done; allow_only = only these sessions; intensity = the most the day may be. A banned session is swapped for the first of its 'instead' sessions that is allowed, otherwise dropped.

limits.name: Train with limits
limits.text: train, but no sprinting or jumping

no_impact.name: No impact
no_impact.text: no impact at all: pool, swimming and upper body only
